content.text:
The local database is not reachable. Both databases that `dev:local` uses refuse connections on `127.0.0.1:6432`.

`services/account/.env.local` points the account service at:

- `DATABASE_URL` — user `nucleum`, database `nucleum_local`, `127.0.0.1:6432`
- `DATAFN_DATABASE_URL` — user `nucleum`, database `nucleum_sync_local`, `127.0.0.1:6432`

A direct Postgres probe of both URLs failed in a few milliseconds with `ECONNREFUSED`. Nothing is listening on port `6432` or `5432`. The running Docker Postgres containers are on other ports (`55433`, `55999`, `55873`, `56543`, `55432`, `5703`), so none of them is the local backend database.

The backend process itself is up. `/tmp/nucleum-backend-local.log` shows it started on port `8787` at `2026-10-03T13:44:15Z`, and `GET /auth/session` returned `200`. That request recorded `dbCallCount: 0`, so it did not touch Postgres. Any request that actually opens a connection will fail until something accepts connections on `127.0.0.1:6432`.

content.text:
The storage was cleared with the container. Nothing left on this machine still holds `nucleum_local` or `nucleum_sync_local`.

I checked every Docker volume that contains Postgres data, including anonymous leftover volumes, and none of them has those database names. There is also no host bind-mount and no Homebrew Postgres cluster with that data. The only stopped Postgres container still on disk is `serro-local-postgres-1`, and that belongs to the reporting project (`devbtidb_local` on port 5432), not this backend.

The account service is still configured in `services/account/.env.local` to use `127.0.0.1:6432`. You can bring up an empty server on that port and recreate the schema. Previous accounts and sync rows will not come back.

From the repo root:

```bash
docker run -d --name nucleum-local-postgres \
  -p 127.0.0.1:6432:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=nucleum \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=nucleum_local \
  postgres:16

docker exec nucleum-local-postgres \
  psql -U nucleum -d nucleum_local -c 'CREATE DATABASE nucleum_sync_local'

npm --workspace @21n/account-service run db:push:local
npm --workspace @21n/account-service run datafn:push:local
```

`dev:local` is already running, so once those two pushes succeed it can open both databases. The first command creates the account database; the second creates the separate DataFn sync database.

<timestamp>Saturday, Oct 3, 2026, 7:32 PM (UTC+5:30)</timestamp>
<user_query>
how to spin up the local docker postgres so that data is separated from container so that even if container is removed - the volume can be used?
</user_query>

Use a named volume. Docker keeps that volume when you remove the container. An unnamed volume is deleted with `docker rm -v`, which is what cleared the last database.

```bash
docker volume create nucleum-local-pg

docker run -d --name nucleum-local-postgres \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:6432:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=nucleum \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=nucleum_local \
  -v nucleum-local-pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16

docker exec nucleum-local-postgres \
  psql -U nucleum -d nucleum_local -c 'CREATE DATABASE nucleum_sync_local'
```

The `-v nucleum-local-pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data` flag is the part that separates the data from the container. Port `6432`, user `nucleum`, and the two database names match `services/account/.env.local`.

On a fresh volume, create the schema once:

```bash
npm --workspace @21n/account-service run db:push:local
npm --workspace @21n/account-service run datafn:push:local
```

If you later remove only the container, start it again with the same volume name. Skip the `CREATE DATABASE` and the two push commands; the data is already in `nucleum-local-pg`.

```bash
docker rm -f nucleum-local-postgres

docker run -d --name nucleum-local-postgres \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -p 127.0.0.1:6432:5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=nucleum \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=nucleum_local \
  -v nucleum-local-pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16
```

`docker rm` and `docker rm -v` leave a named volume in place. The data is removed only by `docker volume rm nucleum-local-pg` or `docker volume prune`.
